h1: Nursing staffing agencies: 10 firms sorted by how they actually fill shifts
seoTitle: Nursing Staffing Agencies: 10 Firms by Staffing Model (2026)
description: Ten nursing staffing agencies grouped by the job they do best: travel contracts, rapid response, per diem apps, franchise networks and international RN pipelines, with where each is based and what to check before you sign.
lead: A director of nursing with three open night shifts and a unit going on a 13 week census spike needs two different agencies, not one. This guide sorts nurse staffing firms by the model they run, so you call the right kind first.
shortAnswer: Short answer: for 13 week travel contracts at scale, start with Aya Healthcare. For a crisis opening or a labor action, Fastaff built the rapid response model. For per diem shifts in skilled nursing and post-acute settings, IntelyCare and Nursefinders are the first calls. If the gap is permanent and structural, the international pipelines at Avant and Conexus MedStaff take a year or more but end with your own employee.

choose.h: Name the model before the firm.
choose.p: Per diem fills a single shift, travel fills roughly a quarter, rapid response fills a gap that opens this week, and international recruitment fills a permanent seat on a long lead time. Most bad agency experiences come from buying one model to solve another.

choose.h: Ask for the certification letter.
choose.p: Several firms below hold The Joint Commission's Health Care Staffing Services certification. Ask for the current letter rather than relying on a logo on the website, and ask how credential files are shared with your compliance team.

choose.h: Get the bill rate structure in writing.
choose.p: Ask whether the quote is an all-in hourly bill rate or a pay rate plus markup, what overtime and holiday multipliers apply, and whether there is a conversion fee if you hire the nurse permanently.

choose.h: Check who your account actually sits with.
choose.p: Several of these firms are now one brand inside a larger group. Ask which entity signs the contract, who handles escalations, and whether a vendor management system or a managed services program sits between you and the agency.

firms.name: Aya Healthcare
firms.model: Travel nursing, per diem app, workforce software
firms.bestFor: Large travel contracts plus the software to manage them
firms.summary: Aya describes itself as America's largest travel nursing and allied health staffing agency. Alongside travel contracts it sells workforce software to hospitals: the LotusOne vendor management system, a Workforce AI demand matching tool, an app-based Shifts product for per diem and float pool work, and CoreHire for permanent hiring.
good: You need many travel nurses across several units or sites
You want agency supply and a VMS from one vendor
watch: If Aya also runs your VMS, ask how other agencies are treated in the order queue
Large accounts get the most attention; small single unit orders may not

firms.name: Fastaff
firms.model: Rapid response travel nursing
firms.bestFor: Urgent openings that cannot wait for a normal travel start date
firms.summary: Fastaff was founded in 1989 and introduced what it calls the Rapid Response model: deploying experienced nurses quickly to hospitals facing urgent shortages, with guaranteed delivery and a focus on hard to fill specialties. It holds The Joint Commission's Gold Seal for staffing and is one of eight brands in the Ingenovis Health group, which also includes Trustaff, USN and VISTA Staffing.
good: A unit needs experienced nurses within days, not weeks
You want one group that can also cover longer travel and labor disruption needs
watch: Rapid response rates are a premium product; budget for it as an exception
Clarify which Ingenovis brand owns the order so escalations go to the right team

firms.name: IntelyCare
firms.model: App based per diem and part-time nursing
firms.bestFor: Skilled nursing and post-acute facilities filling shifts week to week
firms.summary: IntelyCare runs an app that matches nurses and nursing assistants to open shifts, and calls itself a healthcare talent platform rather than a traditional agency. In 2023 it moved to a regional structure and added full-time and part-time hiring alongside shifts. It holds The Joint Commission's Health Care Staffing Services certification.
good: Your gaps are individual shifts in long term care or post-acute settings
Schedulers want to post and fill shifts themselves
watch: Check coverage in your specific region before signing
An app fills shifts, it does not build unit continuity; pair it with a retention plan

firms.name: Nursefinders
firms.model: Per diem and local contract staffing
firms.bestFor: Local per diem coverage backed by a large parent
firms.summary: Nursefinders has placed nurses and allied professionals for more than 40 years and now focuses on per diem and local jobs in nursing, allied health and healthcare support. It is Joint Commission accredited and part of AMN Healthcare, which gives buyers a route into AMN's travel and workforce programs if needs grow.
good: You want local nurses who can pick up recurring shifts
You may later want travel or managed services from the same parent
watch: Local branch strength varies by metro; ask for fill rates in your market
Confirm whether orders route through an AMN program or directly

firms.name: Favorite Healthcare Staffing
firms.model: Per diem, local, travel and permanent placement
firms.bestFor: Facilities that want one vendor across every contract length
firms.summary: Favorite started placing travel nurses in 1991 and now offers per diem, local and travel assignments, temp to perm and direct hire, plus recruitment process outsourcing and a managed services program. It has held The Joint Commission certification since 2005 and says it has appeared on Staffing Industry Analysts' largest healthcare staffing firms list every year since 2009. It describes itself as part of a larger multinational group, with Espirita as its international sister company.
good: You want per diem and travel from one contract
You may outsource part of permanent nurse recruiting later
watch: Ask which parts of the group serve your account
Broad menus can mean thinner specialty depth; ask for references in your specialty

firms.name: ATC Healthcare
firms.model: Franchise network, per diem and contract
firms.bestFor: Local coverage from an owner operated office
firms.summary: ATC Healthcare has run a healthcare staffing franchise for close to 40 years, with locally owned offices across the United States. It serves hospitals, residential care programs, public health departments, school systems, medical groups and municipal governments.
good: You value a local owner you can call directly
Public sector and school nursing needs sit alongside hospital shifts
watch: Quality depends on the local franchise; meet the office that will serve you
Multi-state systems may deal with several franchise owners

firms.name: Gifted Healthcare
firms.model: Travel, local and per diem nursing
firms.bestFor: Gulf South facilities mixing contract lengths
firms.summary: Gifted Healthcare places nurses on travel assignments, local contracts and per diem shifts, and also covers allied health and education based roles such as school nursing and behavioral interventionists.
good: You need RNs, LPNs and CNAs across contract types
School and behavioral roles sit in the same budget as clinical nursing
watch: Confirm specialty depth for ICU, OR and L&D before relying on it
Ask for state by state fill history outside its home region

firms.name: Stability Healthcare
firms.model: Travel nursing and allied, permanent roles
firms.bestFor: Travel RN coverage from a smaller, clinician focused firm
firms.summary: Stability Healthcare places travel registered nurses and allied clinicians, lists permanent jobs alongside contracts, and runs a managed services offering for facilities. Its public job pages publish weekly pay ranges by state, which helps buyers sanity check the rates they are quoted.
good: You want a firm that publishes pay data openly
Med-surg, tele, ICU and ER travel needs
watch: Smaller bench than the national giants for very large orders
Ask how quickly it can credential for your state

firms.name: Avant Healthcare Professionals
firms.model: International nurse recruitment
firms.bestFor: Permanent RN seats filled from overseas
firms.summary: Avant has recruited internationally educated nurses for U.S. health systems for more than 20 years and is a member of the Jackson Healthcare family of companies. It holds The Joint Commission certification and stresses ethical recruitment practices that it says meet or exceed global standards.
good: Vacancies are structural and you can plan a year or more ahead
You want nurses who become long term members of your staff
watch: Immigration timelines are outside the agency's control
Read the commitment period and repayment terms that apply to nurses

firms.name: Conexus MedStaff
firms.model: International nurse recruitment
firms.bestFor: International pipelines with Philippines and UK teams
firms.summary: Conexus MedStaff was founded in Houston in 2011 and is led by CEO Andrew Moreton. It is family owned, with teams in the UK and the Philippines, and guides nurses through immigration, licensure and relocation into U.S. roles.
good: You want a second international pipeline alongside an incumbent
Relocation support matters for retention in your market
watch: Same lead time caveats as any international program
Ask how many nurses it currently has in the visa queue for your specialty

inhouse.h: When your own recruiting team should do it instead
p: Agency nurses solve a capacity problem, but every agency hour costs more than an employed hour, and none of it builds a bench. If the same units call an agency every quarter, the cheaper fix is usually a recruiting function that keeps a warm pipeline of local nurses: a CRM of past applicants and former staff, a scheduler that books interviews quickly, and outreach that reaches nurses on their phones.

Software can carry part of that load. Our high volume hiring stack covers the scheduling and screening side, and the sourcing tools category compares the search layer. Tools such as Noon's nurse sourcing workflow treat licensure as a hard filter and contact clinicians by email and SMS, which is how most nurses prefer to be reached between shifts.

Ask every firm on your shortlist to quote the same scenario: one night shift RN in your busiest unit for 13 weeks, and one per diem shift next Saturday. Comparing the two answers side by side shows you which firms are really travel shops and which are really local shops, regardless of what the website says.

Then ask what happens at week 14. A firm that only talks about extensions is selling continuity; a firm that offers a conversion path is selling you a hire. Both are fine, as long as you know which one you are buying. Our guide to applicant tracking systems covers how to keep agency and direct applicants in one record.

faq.q: What is the difference between a per diem and a travel nursing agency?
faq.a: A per diem agency fills individual shifts with nurses who live locally, often booked a few days ahead. A travel agency places a nurse on a fixed contract, commonly around 13 weeks, usually from outside your area.

faq.q: Do nursing staffing agencies need to be certified?
faq.a: Certification is voluntary, but many hospitals require it. The Joint Commission's Health Care Staffing Services certification is the most common; ask for the current letter during contracting.

faq.q: Can I hire an agency nurse permanently?
faq.a: Usually, but most contracts include a conversion fee or a minimum number of worked hours before conversion. Read that clause before the first shift, not after you want to make an offer.

faq.q: How do I list my staffing firm on this page?
faq.a: Use the listing details at the end of the guide. We review every request against the same criteria as the firms above.

description: Ten staffing agencies in Dallas with a verified office in the metro, from Noel Road and North Central Expressway to Plano, Irving and Garland, sorted by the kind of hire each handles best.
lead: Which Dallas staffing agency should you call? It depends less on the brand and more on the seat: a contract controller, a cybersecurity engineer and forty warehouse pickers are three different phone calls. Every firm below has a staffed office in the Dallas area, and we list the street so you know who is local.
shortAnswer: Short answer: for finance and office roles with a written guarantee, start with Frontline Source Group or Robert Half. For IT contractors at scale, TEKsystems and LaSalle Network. Clinical and revenue cycle roles go to Medix in Irving, and hourly warehouse or call center volume to Snelling. If you want a Texas owned firm, Choice Specialists is the Dallas arm of Burnett Specialists.

choose.h: Decide whether you are buying hours or a hire.
choose.p: Temporary and contract work is priced as an hourly bill rate; direct hire is priced as a fee on first year salary. Ask each firm to quote both for the same role, because the gap tells you how much the firm wants each kind of order.

choose.h: Ask which office will actually work the order.
choose.p: Several national firms serve Dallas from Plano or Irving. That is fine for remote friendly roles, but for on-site interviews or shift work you want the recruiter who knows the commute from Garland to the Stemmons corridor.

choose.h: Get the guarantee terms, not the slogan.
choose.p: Replacement guarantees range from a few weeks to multiple years. Read what triggers a refund or a free replacement, and whether layoffs or role changes void it.

choose.h: Check conversion fees before day one.
choose.p: If a temp might become permanent, ask how many worked hours remove the conversion fee. Texas employers often lose money here simply because nobody asked.

inhouse.h: When Dallas employers should recruit directly
p: The metroplex has one of the deepest professional labor pools in the country, which cuts both ways: candidates are plentiful, but so are competing offers. If you place the same accountant or developer profile through an agency every quarter, those fees would usually fund an internal recruiter within a year.

A lean internal setup needs three things: an applicant tracking system that keeps past applicants searchable, a scheduling tool that books interviews within a day, and a way to reach passive candidates. For active applicants, start with a shortlist of job posting sites rather than posting everywhere. Our staffing agency stack shows what agencies themselves run, and the applicant tracking systems category compares the record keeping layer.

Ask every shortlisted firm the same two questions: what is the bill rate for a contract staff accountant for twelve weeks, and what is the placement fee for a permanent one at your salary band. Firms that answer quickly have the market data; firms that need a week are probably building a quote from scratch.

For light industrial and call center work, ask for the pay rate and the markup separately, and confirm who handles drug screening and background checks. Our background check category covers the vendors agencies typically use.

faq.q: Which staffing agency in Dallas is best for temporary office work?
faq.a: For clerical and administrative temps, Choice Specialists, Robert Half and Snelling all list administrative staffing from Dallas offices. Ask each for its fill time on a one week assignment.

faq.q: Do Plano and Irving offices count as Dallas agencies?
faq.a: For most hiring, yes. Plano and Irving are inside the Dallas metro, and several national firms run their North Texas teams from there.

faq.q: How much do Dallas staffing agencies charge?
faq.a: Contract roles are billed as an hourly rate that includes the worker's pay plus a markup; permanent placements are usually a percentage of first year salary. Rates vary by role, so request written quotes.

faq.q: Can my firm be added to this list?
faq.a: Yes. Use the listing details below; we check every firm's Dallas office before adding it.

faq.q: Is there a Dallas agency that offers payrolling?
faq.a: Choice Specialists lists payrolling services, which lets you put a worker you found yourself on the agency's payroll.

lead: How many staffing firms does a mid-sized employer actually need? Usually two or three, each matched to a different kind of hire. The ten firms below are all national, all still independent brands under the parents named here as of November 2026, and all verified on their own websites this week. They are grouped by what they are built to do, not by revenue, because a firm that fills forklift shifts by the morning is a poor choice for a controller search and the reverse is just as true.
shortAnswer: Short answer: for specialized contract and permanent hires in finance, technology, legal and administration, start with Robert Half. For IT contractors at volume, call Insight Global or Kforce. For locally owned offices in smaller markets, Express Employment Professionals. For same-day industrial and event labor, PeopleReady.

choose.h: Decide whether you are buying hours or a hire.
choose.p: Contract staffing bills an hourly markup for as long as the person works for you; direct hire charges a one-time fee, usually a share of first-year salary. Many firms on this list do both, but most have a center of gravity, and the recruiters you meet will be trained on that side of the business.

choose.h: Match the firm's specialty to the job family.
choose.p: A generalist branch can fill a receptionist role in a day, but a SOX auditor or a Kubernetes engineer needs a recruiter who works that niche every week. Ask how many people in that exact job family the local team placed in the last quarter.

choose.h: Ask who owns the candidate relationship.
choose.p: Franchised networks are run by local owners, so service quality varies by office. Company-owned branches follow one playbook. Neither is better, but you should know which you are signing with before you negotiate terms.

choose.h: Get the conversion terms in writing.
choose.p: If you may hire a contractor permanently, agree the conversion fee and the hours after which it drops before the first person starts. This is the clause most often disputed later.

inhouse.h: When a Phoenix employer should recruit directly

When the same roles open every month, the math changes. A company that converts most of its temps after ninety days is effectively paying the agency to recruit permanent staff, and a full time recruiter often costs less within a year.

The internal setup does not need to be elaborate. An applicant tracking system with text messaging, a referral bonus that is paid quickly and a standing relationship with one or two agencies for overflow covers most Valley employers. A recruiter on your own team who sources from those lists, plus a clear job description that names the permits and programs the role owns, can fill steady roles without a fee.

The tooling for that is simpler than it was. An AI sourcing tool can build a list of certified safety professionals in a region, and interview scheduling software cuts the delay between a reply and a plant visit. Keep agencies for the senior searches and the urgent contract cover where their networks pay off.

Murray Resources and Core Group Resources are the two Houston firms most suited to individual direct hires. Murray covers office and technical roles across the energy sector, while Core Group is the pick for offshore, vessel and Jones Act work.

inhouse.h: When to hire in Houston without an agency
p: Agencies earn their fee on speed and on carrying payroll risk. If you hire the same office or technical role several times a year, an in house recruiter with a job board budget and a referral program will often cost less than repeated direct hire fees. Houston's university pipeline from the University of Houston, Rice and Texas Southern helps for early career roles, and our applicant tracking systems category lists the tools that keep those applicants organized.

For harder searches, sourcing software can do the first pass that an agency researcher would. Some staffing firms in the city already run that way, using AI sourcing built for staffing firms such as Noon, which finds candidates and contacts them by email and SMS. Employers can do the same, then keep agencies for shift coverage and urgent backfills. Our staffing agency tool stack shows what a lean setup looks like.

sections.h: Office locations by part of town
p: Uptown and the Galleria hold the densest cluster: Robert Half and Insight Global both sit on Post Oak Boulevard, and Murray Resources keeps a Galleria location on San Felipe. PrideStaff's southwest franchise is on Augusta Drive a short drive away. Downtown, Addison Group is on Lamar Street and Murray has an office on Smith Street. Vaco is at Greenway Plaza, Burnett Specialists anchors Westchase on Richmond Avenue, and Murray's main office is on Gessner Road in Memorial.

West and north of the Beltway, Robert Half covers the Energy Corridor from the Katy Freeway, PrideStaff's northwest franchise is on Jones Road, and Express runs a Houston North office on West Road. Professional Alternatives and Murray both list suburban branches, from Katy and Spring to The Woodlands, Kingwood, Sugar Land and League City.

Agencies quote temporary staff as a bill rate: the worker's hourly pay plus a markup that covers payroll taxes, workers' compensation, benefits and margin. Light industrial markups are usually lower in percentage terms than professional contractors, but injury coverage moves the number. Direct hire fees are a share of first year salary. None of the nine firms publish rates, so ask every shortlisted agency for a written quote on the same role, the same hours and the same guarantee period, and compare the totals rather than the percentages.

We started from firms that advertise staffing in Houston, then opened each firm's own Houston or locations page on November 14, 2026, following redirects and reading the page title to confirm the current brand. Only firms with a published Houston area address made the cut, and every address and specialty above comes from those pages. Nobody paid for placement. For other Texas metros see our guides to staffing agencies in Dallas and staffing agencies in San Antonio.

faq.q: Which staffing agency in Houston is best for office temps?
faq.a: Burnett Specialists and Professional Alternatives both started in Texas and focus heavily on office, accounting and administrative roles. Burnett's headquarters is in Westchase; Professional Alternatives was founded in Houston in 1998 and has suburban branches.

faq.q: Which agencies handle warehouse and light industrial work in Houston?
faq.a: Express Employment Professionals and PrideStaff both run Houston franchise offices that list light industrial, warehouse and skilled trades staffing. Pick the office closest to your facility, since franchises set their own terms.

faq.q: Do Houston staffing agencies charge job seekers?
faq.a: No. Legitimate staffing agencies are paid by the employer through a bill rate or a placement fee. A firm that asks a candidate to pay to be placed is not operating as a normal staffing agency.

faq.q: How long does it take a Houston agency to fill a temporary role?
faq.a: Shift roles in warehouses or call centers are often filled within a day or two when the agency already has workers on file. Professional contractors such as accountants or developers usually take several days to a couple of weeks, depending on the skill set.

faq.q: What is the difference between temp to hire and direct hire?
faq.a: With temp to hire, the worker starts on the agency's payroll and you can convert them after a set period, sometimes with a conversion fee. With direct hire, the person joins your payroll on day one and you pay the agency a one time placement fee.

faq.a: Yes. We review firms every month. Email us with your firm name, website and the Houston office address shown on your own site.

h1: Restaurant headhunters: 8 firms compared by the level they hire and how they charge
seoTitle: Restaurant Headhunters: 8 Search Firms Compared (2026)
description: Eight restaurant headhunters checked in November 2026, sorted by the jobs they actually fill (multi-unit and executive versus store level managers and chefs), how each one charges and where it is based.
lead: A franchisee with eleven units loses a director of operations in October, right before the holiday rush, and a posting on the usual job boards brings in line cooks and shift leads instead of anyone who has run a district. That gap is the reason restaurant headhunters exist. We checked each firm below on its own website on November 15, 2026, noted the level of role it says it fills, where it is based and how it works, and left out names whose domains no longer belong to a recruiting business.
shortAnswer: Short answer: for a C suite or vice president search at a restaurant group, talk to The Elliot Group first and compare it with Horizon Hospitality. For general managers, executive chefs and directors of operations at independent and multi concept groups, JWB Hospitality and Hospitality Confidential are the closest fit. When you need many store level managers across several states, the franchise networks at Gecko Hospitality and Patrice & Associates have the reach. Goodwin Recruiting suits operators who want one firm for restaurant and corporate roles, and Chefs Recruit is a niche choice for culinary placements.

choose.h: Match the firm to the level of the hire.
choose.p: A firm that runs retained searches for chief operating officers rarely wants a single assistant manager opening, and a high volume manager recruiter may not have the board level network for a CEO search. Tell each firm the title, the unit count the person will oversee and the salary band before anything else.

choose.h: Ask whether the recruiter has worked a line or run a store.
choose.p: Several firms on this list say their recruiters came out of restaurant operations. That background shows up in the screening call: someone who has closed a P&L at month end asks better questions about food cost, labor percentage and turnover than a generalist reading a job description.

choose.h: Get the fee model in writing.
choose.p: Contingency firms are paid only when you hire, usually a percentage of first year base salary. Retained firms take part of the fee up front and commit a team to the search. JWB Hospitality publishes its contingency rate on its site; most others quote per search, so ask for the percentage, the guarantee period and what counts toward base.

choose.h: Find out how they reach people who are not looking.
choose.p: The best general managers are usually busy running a strong store. Ask each firm how it approaches passive candidates, how it keeps your search confidential and how many people it expects to present in the first two weeks.

watch: Private service is a large share of its work, so it is not a general restaurant search firm

inhouse.h: When to fill a restaurant management role yourself
p: A headhunter's fee on a $75,000 general manager is real money, and it is hard to justify when your own pipeline is healthy. Promote from within first: an assistant general manager who already knows your systems ramps faster than anyone a firm can find. Referral bonuses paid to your current managers also work well, since good operators tend to know other good operators.

For outside hires, an applicant tracking system keeps every past applicant searchable, so last year's runner up for a GM role is one search away. Teams that want to reach passive managers directly can add a sourcing tool; AI sourcing products such as Noon find candidates and contact them by email and SMS, which is often enough for store level openings. Keep the headhunter for executive searches, confidential replacements and new market openings where you have no network.

The eight firms split into two groups. The Elliot Group, Horizon Hospitality and JWB Hospitality spend most of their time on leadership: chief executives, operations vice presidents, directors of operations and culinary directors. Hospitality Confidential, Gecko Hospitality and Patrice & Associates do more of their work at general manager, assistant manager and multi unit level, where a chain may need a dozen hires a quarter.

Fees are usually a percentage of the first year base salary. JWB Hospitality is the only firm here that prints its rate (20% on contingency). Retained firms bill in stages and charge whether or not you hire from their slate, in exchange for a dedicated team and a defined timeline. Whatever the model, ask for the guarantee period: if a placed manager leaves in the first 90 days, a good firm replaces them at no cost.

faq.q: What does a restaurant headhunter do?
faq.a: A restaurant headhunter finds and screens candidates for management, culinary and executive roles at restaurant companies, usually by approaching people who already hold similar jobs. The firm is paid by the employer, not the candidate.

faq.q: Which restaurant headhunters handle executive searches?
faq.a: Of the firms on this page, The Elliot Group runs retained executive search for restaurant and foodservice companies, Horizon Hospitality covers executive and mid management roles, and JWB Hospitality fills C suite, operations and culinary leadership roles on contingency.

faq.q: How much do restaurant recruiters charge?
faq.a: Most charge a percentage of first year base salary. JWB Hospitality lists 20% on contingency with no fee unless you hire; other firms quote per search, so ask for the rate and the guarantee period in writing.

faq.q: Can a headhunter help me hire hourly restaurant staff?
faq.a: Generally no. The firms here focus on salaried managers, chefs and executives. For servers, cooks and other hourly roles, a staffing agency or high volume hiring software is a better fit.

faq.q: Do candidates pay restaurant recruiters?
faq.a: No. Reputable restaurant headhunters are paid by the hiring company, and candidates should never be asked for a placement fee.

inhouse.h: When to recruit in Atlanta without an agency

Atlanta's university pipeline, from Georgia Tech and Georgia State to Emory and Kennesaw State, is strong for early career office and technical hires, and a simple applicant tracking system keeps those applicants from slipping through.

Keep agencies for what they do best: carrying payroll and injury risk on hourly work, covering spikes, and finding specialists quickly. Our staffing agency tool stack shows the software many Atlanta firms run, which is also a useful checklist when you assess an agency's process.

Ask every shortlisted firm to quote the same role, schedule and guarantee period, and compare the total cost per hour worked rather than the headline percentage.

h1: Pharmaceutical headhunters: 8 firms sorted by the seat you need filled
seoTitle: Pharmaceutical Headhunters: 8 Search Firms Compared (2026)
description: Eight pharmaceutical headhunters checked on their own websites in November 2026, grouped by whether they fill board and C suite seats, functional leaders or specialist and contract roles, with locations and service models.
lead: Which firm do you call when a Phase III program loses its head of clinical operations, and is it the same firm you call for a new chief commercial officer? Usually not. Pharmaceutical headhunters split cleanly by the level of role they fill, and picking the wrong tier wastes a month. We read each firm below on its own website on November 16, 2026, noted its service model, where it is based and what it says it does, and dropped firms whose old domains now point somewhere else.
shortAnswer: Short answer: for a chief executive or board search, compare Coulter Partners and Odgers. For vice president and director leaders in commercial, medical or R&D at mid sized drug makers, Klein Hersh and The Bowdoin Group are the closest fit, and Bowdoin can staff a whole function before a launch. For specialists and contractors in clinical, regulatory, safety and biometrics, talk to Proclinical, Barrington James or R&D Partners. ZRG Partners suits a company that wants search plus interim or embedded recruiters at once.

choose.h: Decide the tier before you call anyone.
choose.p: Board and CEO searches are retained, slow and expensive by design. Director level searches in medical affairs or market access often run on contingency. Contract statisticians and clinical research associates are a staffing purchase. Each firm on this list is strongest in one of those three tiers.

choose.h: Test therapeutic area knowledge on the first call.
choose.p: Ask the recruiter to name three people who have run a launch in your indication, or two companies that recently cut a team with the skills you need. A specialist answers in minutes; a generalist promises to get back to you.

choose.h: Check for conflicts with your competitors.
choose.p: Search firms usually agree not to recruit from current clients for a period. If a firm works for most of your rivals, its off limits list may cover the very people you want. Ask for the list before signing.

choose.h: Price the whole engagement.
choose.p: Retained search typically bills a share of first year cash compensation in stages, while contract staffing is a markup on an hourly rate. Ask what happens if the search stalls, how long the replacement guarantee lasts and whether sign on bonuses count toward the fee.

firms.name: Klein Hersh
firms.model: Executive search with an interim staffing arm
firms.bestFor: Commercial, medical and R&D leadership at drug makers and pharma services companies on the East Coast
firms.summary: Klein Hersh has run searches since 1998 and calls itself a precision executive search firm for life sciences and healthcare. Its practice areas are split into pharma and biotech, pharma services and technology, healthcare, and venture capital and private equity, and it also places interim staff. Hunt Scanlon Media has named it one of its top 50 search firms.
good: Pharma services and technology is its own practice, useful for CROs and commercialization vendors
Based in the suburban Philadelphia pharma corridor

Interim staffing is a smaller part of the business; ask about bench depth

firms.hq: London headquarters; US offices in Boston, New York, Philadelphia and San Diego

firms.summary: Proclinical describes itself as a growth partner for life sciences companies, combining executive search, workforce solutions and staffing with a consulting unit that advises on developing, registering and launching products. It lists offices in Europe, North America and Asia Pacific, and in September 2026 it published a case study on filling 12 medical affairs roles across the US in six weeks through its Proclinical Lens program.
good: Covers both one off searches and multi hire team builds
Contract and permanent under one roof, plus regulatory consulting
watch: Large firm, so ask who on the desk actually knows your therapeutic area
Consulting and recruiting are separate services with separate fees

firms.model: Retained executive search and team builds
firms.bestFor: Venture and private equity backed biotechs hiring C suite leaders or building a whole function before a launch

It offers executive search, a strategic search service for leaders below the executive level, and team builds tied to a launch or scale up, and it works closely with investors. The firm cites more than 30 years in business and more than 12,500 placements.
good: Team build service suits a company staffing a commercial organization from scratch
Investor relationships help with portfolio company searches
watch: Healthcare services is a large share of its work, so confirm recent pharma placements
Retained model means an engagement fee up front

It offers direct hire, contract and interim placements and a separate board and executive search service.
good: Functional desks are listed in detail, so you can ask for the specialist team by name
Contract and interim cover for trial peaks
watch: Breadth across medtech and health tech means pharma is one of many desks
Fee terms vary by service; get them in writing per role

firms.bestFor: Sponsors and CROs that want contractors or a functional service provider model for clinical, biometrics or safety work

good: FSP and MSP options when you want a provider to own a whole function
Long track record under the previous Hobson Prior name

firms.hq: Global firm; see its geographic reach page for offices

Its pharma and biotech page says it has served the sector for two decades and claims the largest specialist team doing so. Alongside search it runs board advisory and leadership consulting, and its news page reports recent chief executive placements at biopharma companies.
good: Board advisory and CEO search from the same firm
Specialist focus rather than one practice inside a generalist
watch: Built for the top of the organization only
Global coverage can mean the lead partner sits outside the US

firms.model: Executive search, interim leaders, embedded recruiting and assessments
firms.hq: US offices include Boston, Fort Washington, Pennsylvania and New York City
firms.bestFor: Pharma companies that want one firm for an executive search plus interim cover or embedded recruiters during a reorganization
firms.summary: ZRG runs a healthcare and life sciences practice inside a broader talent firm. Its menu includes executive search, interim and fractional leaders, embedded recruiting teams, assessments, coaching and outplacement, so a client can combine a permanent search with a stopgap leader or a recruiting team that sits inside the company for a period.
good: Interim and embedded options next to search
Assessment services for validating finalists
watch: Life sciences is one of several industry groups
Ask for pharma specific references rather than general healthcare ones

firms.model: Executive search, interim management and leadership advisory
firms.hq: International firm with a US practice; offices listed on its site
firms.bestFor: Board seats, CEOs and enterprise functional leaders at large pharmaceutical groups
firms.summary: Odgers has a dedicated life sciences executive search page within its life sciences and healthcare group. The firm also sells board and CEO services, board succession, interim management and leadership assessment, which suits a pharma company planning succession for several senior roles rather than filling a single seat.
good: Board and succession services for large companies
Interim management when a leader leaves suddenly
watch: Generalist firm, so confirm the partner on your search is a life sciences specialist
Pricing is per engagement and not published

p: Coulter Partners and Odgers sit at the top: chief executives, board directors and global heads of function, where the firm advises on the role as much as it fills it. Klein Hersh, The Bowdoin Group and ZRG Partners work mostly with vice presidents and directors, and Bowdoin and ZRG can add team builds or interim leaders. Proclinical, Barrington James and R&D Partners do the high volume specialist work, including contractors for trial peaks and outsourced functional teams.

sections.h: Pharma headhunters versus life sciences staffing
p: A pharma headhunter approaches people who are not looking, usually for one senior role at a time. A life sciences staffing firm fills many roles quickly from candidates who are active or already on its contractor bench. Several firms here do both, so say which one you are buying. For broader lists, see our pages on staffing and recruiting firms and nursing staffing agencies.

sections.h: How we chose and checked these firms
p: We included firms whose own sites describe a pharmaceutical or biotech practice, then visited each site on November 16, 2026, followed redirects and noted the current name and parent. Hobson Prior now redirects to R&D Partners, so it appears under its new name. Facts about locations and services come only from each firm's pages. Order follows the tiers above, not a quality score, and no firm paid to appear.

inhouse.h: When to recruit pharma talent in house
p: Not every opening needs a 25 percent fee. Clinical research associates, quality specialists and medical science liaisons are hired in large numbers, and a recruiter with a good applicant tracking system can rediscover past finalists for most of them. Alumni of acquired or downsized companies are another strong pool, since many still list their former employer.

To reach passive specialists directly, add a sourcing tool. AI sourcing products such as Noon for biotech and pharma hiring search beyond LinkedIn and contact candidates through personalized email and SMS, which covers many director and below roles. Keep a headhunter for confidential replacements, board seats and roles where only a few dozen people in the world qualify.

faq.q: What does a pharmaceutical headhunter charge?
faq.a: Retained executive search is usually billed as a percentage of first year compensation in installments, and contingency search is paid only when you hire. Contract staffing is billed as an hourly markup. None of the eight firms here publishes a standard rate, so ask for the percentage, the guarantee period and the payment schedule.

faq.q: How long does a pharma executive search take?
faq.a: Board and C suite searches commonly run three to six months from kickoff to signed offer, longer if the candidate has a long notice period or a non compete. Director searches and contract placements are much faster.

faq.q: Which pharmaceutical headhunters are based near Philadelphia or Boston?
faq.a: Klein Hersh is in Horsham, Pennsylvania, and The Bowdoin Group is in downtown Boston. Proclinical lists offices in both cities, and ZRG Partners lists Boston and Fort Washington, Pennsylvania.

faq.q: Is Hobson Prior still operating?
faq.a: Its website now redirects to R&D Partners, which says it is the same team under a new brand, part of Acacium Group.

faq.q: Should I use a headhunter or a staffing firm for clinical trial roles?
faq.a: Use a staffing or functional service provider when you need several contract roles fast, such as clinical research associates for a study start. Use a headhunter for the permanent leader who will run the program.

inhouse.h: When to hire in Jacksonville without an agency
p: If you hire the same role every month, the fees add up. h1: Aerospace staffing agencies: 10 firms sorted by the kind of aerospace hire you need
seoTitle: Aerospace Staffing Agencies: 10 Firms Checked (2026)
description: Ten aerospace staffing agencies checked on November 17, 2026, grouped by what they actually fill: engineering programs, shop floor trades, maintenance contractors, business aviation crews and cleared defense roles, with the headquarters and parent company each firm lists.
lead: Is your opening on a design program, a production line, a hangar floor or a flight department? Those are four different recruiting markets, and most aerospace agencies are strong in only one or two of them. We opened every firm's own site on November 17, 2026 and sorted them by the work they say they staff.
shortAnswer: Short answer: for engineering programs, start with Actalent or Belcan. For assemblers, avionics and sheet metal technicians, call PDS Tech Commercial. For contract aircraft maintenance crews, Strom Aviation is the specialist, and for pilots and flight department leaders, Aviation Personnel International. Defense contractors that need cleared staff should add TAD PGS or Moseley Technical Services to the shortlist.

choose.h: Decide which market the role sits in.
choose.p: A stress engineer, a composite technician and a charter captain share an industry but almost nothing else. Ask each agency how many people it placed in your exact job family last year, not how many aerospace clients it has.

choose.h: Ask about clearances and export control before price.
choose.p: If the work touches defense programs or controlled technical data, confirm the firm can recruit people who already hold the clearance level you need and that its own staff are set up to handle controlled job details. Starting a clearance from zero adds months.

choose.h: Check whether you are buying contract labor or a search.
choose.p: Several firms below put contractors on their own payroll for the length of a program, while others run direct hire or retained searches and charge a placement fee. Mixing the two models in one contract usually means one of them is done badly.

choose.h: Ask where the recruiters sit.
choose.p: Maintenance and production talent is local. A firm with a desk near your plant or hangar will know which shops are laying off and which are poaching. Engineering searches travel better, so a national desk is fine there.

choose.h: Get the certification check in writing.
choose.p: For technicians, the agency should confirm FAA certificates and any OEM training before a candidate reaches you, and say who pays if a contractor turns out not to hold what was claimed.

inhouse.h: When to recruit aerospace talent yourself
p: Agencies earn their fee on surges, cleared roles and leadership searches. For steady technician hiring, an in house pipeline is usually cheaper: Part 147 aviation maintenance schools, community college composites and machining programs and military transition offices all produce candidates every term, and a recruiter who visits them twice a year builds a bench no agency can match.

Engineering roles that repeat every quarter are also worth bringing in house. Keep a list of former contractors who did good work, stay in touch between programs and reuse your strongest job postings. Our guide to staffing and recruiting firms explains how the contract and direct hire models compare if you plan to split the work.

sections.h: Contract, direct hire or a program team
p: Most aerospace hiring falls into three buying models. Contract staffing puts the worker on the agency's payroll and suits programs with a known end date. Direct hire or retained search ends with the person on your payroll, and the fee is a share of first year pay. A program team, which Actalent, Belcan and Akkodis all offer in some form, means the vendor delivers a defined scope of engineering work and manages its own people.

Pick the model per role, not per vendor. Buying a design package as a service while contracting technicians and running your own leadership searches is common, and it keeps each agency doing what it is best at.

Moseley sits in Huntsville next to missile and space work, Strom has an office in the Fort Worth area, PDS is based in Irving in the same metro, and API is in Savannah, home to a large business jet maker. faq.a: Aviation Personnel International focuses on business and private aviation, including pilots and directors of aviation, and also offers compensation benchmarking.

faq.q: Are aerospace recruiters different from engineering recruiters?
faq.a: Often yes. General engineering firms can fill mechanical and manufacturing roles, but aerospace specialists know FAA and DoD quality rules, certificate checks and the program cycles that drive hiring.

choose.p: Port, distribution and manufacturing employers along I 95 need firms that can fill twenty shifts by Monday. Hospitals, universities and federal contractors usually need two or three specialists. Very few branches do both well, so do not expect one agency to cover the whole building.

choose.h: Bring a markup ceiling to the first call.
choose.p: Temporary staff are billed as an hourly rate that includes the worker's pay plus the agency's markup for payroll taxes, insurance and margin. Know the most you will pay per hour before you hear a quote, and ask for it in writing for each job title.

choose.h: Check clearance and contract experience if you work with the government.
choose.p: Fort Meade, the Social Security Administration in Woodlawn and the defense contractors around them create demand for cleared IT and engineering people. choose.h: Read the conversion clause.

inhouse.h: When to recruit clinical staff yourself
p: Agencies make sense for surge capacity and hard to reach geographies. For a steady pipeline of study coordinators or a second CRA in a city where you already run sites, an internal recruiter with a clean shortlist process is usually cheaper over a year.

Clinical professionals are reachable: most list certifications such as ACRP or SOCRA credentials and their therapeutic areas on public profiles, and many respond to a short, specific email naming the protocol phase and travel load. Teams that want help with the reach out step can use tools that find and contact candidates through personalized email and SMS sequences for biotech roles, then keep agencies for the requisitions that stall.

Whichever route you choose, write the job around the study rather than the title. A CRA posting that states the number of sites, the visit cadence and the remote versus onsite split attracts more qualified replies than one that lists generic GCP knowledge.

sections.h: Contract, FSP or CRO: what you are really buying
p: The nine firms fall into three groups. Planet Pharma, Kelly Science and Clinical, The Fountain Group and Barrington James mostly place individuals, either as contractors on the firm's payroll or as direct hires. ClinLab Solutions Group, R&D Partners and Actalent sell both individual placements and functional service programs. Advanced Clinical and ClinChoice are CROs whose FSP and resourcing teams compete with staffing firms for the same budgets.

That split matters because the risk sits in different places. With a contractor, you own the training, the oversight and the quality of monitoring reports. With an FSP, the provider owns those, and you own the governance meeting. With a CRO resourcing team, the staff may be more experienced, but they can be reassigned to the CRO's own projects when your contract ends, so plan for transitions.

If you are comparing this list with broader pharmaceutical headhunters, the difference is scope: headhunters place permanent leaders across commercial, medical and research functions, while the firms here are built around study execution.

sections.h: What to ask on the first call
p: Ask for the number of CRAs the firm has on active assignments today, the share that are home based, and how many it placed in your therapeutic area in the last year. Ask how it checks GCP training and prior monitoring experience, and whether it verifies degrees and certifications itself or relies on the candidate.

For FSP proposals, ask who writes the performance metrics, how often they are reported, and what happens when a team member leaves mid study. A good provider will name a backfill window and the person accountable for it.

Finally, ask how the firm handles a candidate who is also being submitted by another supplier on your vendor list. Duplicate submissions are common in clinical staffing, and the master agreement should say which supplier owns the candidate.

Two clusters stand out. Horsham appears twice for unrelated reasons: Barrington James is headquartered in Horsham, England, while ClinChoice lists its international headquarters in Horsham, Pennsylvania, north of Philadelphia. The Chicago area has Planet Pharma and Advanced Clinical, the second in Deerfield. Boston biotech buyers have ClinLab Solutions Group in Watertown, and Research Triangle sponsors can meet Barrington James in downtown Raleigh.

Location matters less for contract monitors, who are usually home based, but it still shapes which sites a firm knows. If your network is regional, start with the firm closest to it; for a nationwide program, compare the national suppliers and check their benches city by city. For hospital based research nurses, a nursing staffing agency may move faster than a clinical research specialist.

faq.q: What does a clinical research staffing agency do?
faq.a: It supplies people to run clinical trials: clinical research associates who monitor sites, clinical trial assistants, study coordinators, clinical project managers, data managers and regulatory staff. Some place individual contractors or direct hires; others deliver a managed functional service team.

faq.q: What is an FSP in clinical research?
faq.a: A functional service provider runs one function of a study, such as monitoring or data management, with its own managed team under the sponsor's processes. Actalent, Advanced Clinical, ClinChoice, ClinLab Solutions Group and R&D Partners all publish FSP offers.

faq.a: Yes. R&D Partners says Hobson Prior is now R&D Partners with the same team and service, and it is part of Acacium Group.

faq.q: Should a small biotech use a CRO or a staffing agency?
faq.a: If you have an internal clinical lead who can supervise contractors, a staffing agency is usually cheaper. If you have no clinical operations team yet, a CRO or FSP provider brings processes and oversight along with the people.

choose.h: Ask which automotive programs the recruiter has filled in the last year.
choose.p: A firm that places mechanical design engineers for a supplier in Troy may have nobody who understands functional safety or battery management software. Ask for job titles, not logos, and for the number of contractors currently on automotive assignments.

choose.h: Check who owns the brand before you sign two contracts.
choose.p: Akkodis and PDS Tech Commercial both link to the Adecco Group code of conduct, and Belcan now describes itself as a Cognizant company. If you already have a master agreement with a parent, a second brand may be able to work under it.

choose.h: Price conversions and launch surges separately.
choose.p: Vehicle launches create short peaks of demand. Ask for the bill rate during a surge, the notice period to release contractors after launch, and the fee or hours required to convert a contractor to a permanent hire.

firms.name: Bartech Staffing
firms.parent: Vertage (the site says Bartech is now powered by Vertage)
firms.model: Engineering, technical and professional staffing
firms.bestFor: Automotive manufacturers and suppliers hiring mechanical engineers and automotive software developers
firms.summary: Bartech says it grew from a foundation in automotive and engineering before moving into other industries, and it claims five decades in talent services. Its automotive page describes a network of professionals in automotive engineering and technical specialties, from mechanical engineers to software developers working on vehicle technology, and it points to supply chain shifts and demand for smarter mobility as the work it staffs. The job seeker side advertises assignments with automotive brands.
good: Automotive is a named market with its own page
Covers engineering and software roles in one firm

Plant labor is not the focus

firms.bestFor: OEMs and heavy vehicle makers that want components, controls or emissions work delivered

Can take ownership of a scoped engineering package

Light on production and plant floor roles

For automotive buyers the appeal is scale close to the industry's home market, plus a division that recruits only engineers.

Engineering division with its own recruiters
watch: Large national firm, so ask who your day to day recruiter is
Automotive is one industry among many

A Troy firm with a quality practice is a natural fit for supplier quality engineers, launch support and PPAP work around the Big Three.
good: Headquartered in the heart of the supplier base
Quality engineering is a named practice
watch: Smaller bench outside Michigan
Check whether a role is staffed or delivered as a project

firms.model: Engineering and product development services
firms.bestFor: Automakers outsourcing EV, embedded and ADAS engineering
firms.summary: Tata Technologies helps automakers design, engineer and validate vehicles, and its automotive page lists turnkey electric vehicle engineering, product benchmarking, rightweighting, simulation and validation, embedded systems, AUTOSAR and hardware in the loop testing, plus connected and autonomous vehicle work. Its about page notes a Frost and Sullivan recognition for production ready ADAS and autonomous engineering. This is a services partner for a program, not an agency that sends resumes.
good: Full vehicle and EV program capability
Strong in embedded software and validation
watch: Not a fit for single contractor requests
Engagements are scoped projects with longer sales cycles

firms.model: Engineering and digital consulting with talent services
firms.bestFor: Teams working on software defined vehicles, electrification and digital twins
firms.summary: Akkodis presents its automotive and transportation practice around software defined vehicles, electrification across automotive, rail and maritime systems, data and digital engineering, and simulation with digital twins. Buyers who want software and systems engineers with vehicle context, or a consulting team that can design and prototype, will find both here.
good: Covers vehicle software, electrification and simulation
Part of a group with very wide reach
watch: Consulting and staffing sit side by side, so be clear which you are buying
Shares a parent with PDS Tech Commercial

firms.model: Skilled trades and engineering staffing
firms.bestFor: Plants and service operations hiring maintenance technicians, electricians and engineers
firms.summary: PDS Tech Commercial describes itself as a skilled trades and engineering workforce provider for high demand industries, and its site links to Adecco Group policies. For automotive buyers the useful part is the trades side: maintenance, electrical and production support roles that keep a plant running between model years. Ask for the branch that covers your plant, because coverage is national.
good: Skilled trades and engineering under one brand
Backed by a large group for volume needs
watch: Automotive is not called out as a separate practice
Same parent as Akkodis, so consolidate terms if you use both

firms.bestFor: Production, maintenance and EV battery plant staffing
firms.summary: Founded in 1983, Aerotek staffs consumer and industrial products employers and describes manufacturing and production workforce solutions. good: Large bench for production and maintenance roles
Offers managed services as well as staffing
watch: Engineering design roles are usually handled elsewhere in its group
National scale, so ask about local fill rates

firms.hq: 90 plus branches across the United States

It lists mechanical, design and project engineers among the roles it fills and says it has more than 90 local branches and 70 years in business. The light industrial side covers production shifts.
good: Engineering heritage plus a light industrial branch network
One vendor for two very different role types
watch: Automotive is not a stand alone practice
Confirm the nearest branch actually recruits engineers

firms.name: PEAK Technical Staffing
firms.model: Technical staffing, MSP programs and payroll services
firms.bestFor: Engineering and manufacturing contractors with payrolling or MSP support
firms.summary: PEAK says it has more than 50 years of industry experience and offers temporary staff augmentation, temp to hire, permanent placement, managed service provider programs and payroll services. It recruits for engineering, manufacturing and IT, and the site promotes total talent programs that cover onboarding and retention. Automotive suppliers that already know who they want to hire can use its payrolling to bring them on quickly.
good: Payrolling for contractors you sourced yourself
MSP programs for larger buyers
watch: Automotive specifics are not spelled out on the site
Generalist technical focus

inhouse.h: When to hire automotive talent yourself
p: Agencies make sense for launch surges and for scarce profiles such as functional safety or battery systems engineers. Recurring hires are different. If you replace the same quality technician every quarter, a referral program and a quick interview loop usually beat paying markup on every hour.

Experienced vehicle engineers rarely answer job posts, so in house teams increasingly search for them directly. The tools in our sourcing tools category help with that, from contact finders to AI platforms such as Noon that run personalized email and SMS outreach. Compare a month of that against one placement fee before you choose.
Contract engineering: Bartech, Kelly Engineering, RGBSI and Nesco place individual engineers and technicians on your team. You manage the work and pay an hourly bill rate.

Engineering services: Belcan, Tata Technologies and Akkodis take responsibility for a scope such as validation, embedded software or a powertrain package. You pay for the outcome, often with milestones. Our list of aerospace staffing agencies covers several of the same firms on the flight side.

Plant and trades staffing: PDS Tech Commercial, Aerotek and Nesco's light industrial branches fill production, maintenance and electrical roles. For electricians alone, see our electrical staffing agencies list.

sections.h: Questions to ask every automotive agency
p: How many contractors do you have on automotive assignments today, and in which job titles? Who will recruit for us, and how many open orders does that person carry? Which tools and standards do your candidates know, for example CATIA, NX, AUTOSAR or ISO 26262?

What happens to bill rates during a launch, and how much notice do you need to roll contractors off? What is the conversion fee, and after how many hours does it fall to zero? For a wider view of how agencies price, read our guide to staffing and recruiting firms.

faq.q: What does an automotive staffing agency do?
faq.a: It supplies contract, temp to hire or permanent workers to automakers, suppliers and dealers. Most specialize in either engineering and technical roles or plant, maintenance and skilled trades roles.

faq.q: Which automotive staffing agencies are based in Michigan?
faq.a: Kelly Services lists its headquarters in Troy, Michigan, and RGBSI lists its world headquarters on Stephenson Highway in Troy. Several national firms on this list also recruit in the Detroit area.

faq.q: Is an engineering services firm the same as a staffing agency?
faq.a: No. A staffing agency lends you people you manage. An engineering services firm such as Belcan or Tata Technologies delivers a defined piece of work and manages its own engineers.

faq.q: Who staffs EV battery plants?
faq.a: Production and maintenance roles at battery plants are often filled by large industrial staffing firms. Aerotek, for example, describes a maintenance reliability program it built for an EV battery startup.

faq.q: How do I get my automotive staffing firm added to this list?
faq.a: Use the listing form on this page. We check every firm's own website before adding it and update the list as firms change names or owners.

h1: Staffing agencies in Louisville: 6 firms with offices we confirmed, from downtown to Hurstbourne
seoTitle: Staffing Agencies in Louisville, KY: 6 Offices Verified (2026)
description: Six staffing agencies with a Louisville office confirmed on their own websites on November 20, 2026: street address, what each one recruits, parent company and which to call for plant, office, IT or nursing hires.
lead: A distribution center near the airport needs forty pickers before peak season, and the accounting team downtown needs a payables specialist by Monday. Those are different calls in Louisville, and the firms that answer them sit in different parts of town. We opened each agency's own location page on November 20, 2026 and kept six firms that publish a Louisville office or headquarters. Four of them cluster in the 40222 ZIP code along Shelbyville Road, Hurstbourne Parkway and Bullitt Lane in the east end, one is downtown on South Fifth Street, and one is a Louisville founded company with its headquarters on Campus Place.
shortAnswer: Short answer: warehouse, construction and maintenance crews go to Aerotek or Malone. Developers and help desk contractors fit TEKsystems. Payables, payroll and admin roles fit Robert Half or Vaco. Travel and facility nurses come through Malone's healthcare desk, and employers who want one firm across many departments can try Insight Global downtown.

choose.h: Start with the shift, not the brand.
choose.p: Second and third shift work in Jefferson County is mostly industrial, and the agencies that fill it keep a bench of people who already work nights. Ask how many associates the branch placed on overnight shifts last quarter before you compare rates.

choose.h: Check who the parent company is.
choose.p: TEKsystems and Aerotek are both Allegis Group companies and both sit in the same east end ZIP code. Vaco now operates under the Highspring name. Knowing the parent helps you avoid signing two master agreements with what is effectively one supplier.

choose.h: Ask for the conversion clause in writing.
choose.p: Most temp to hire contracts let you keep a worker without a fee after a set number of paid hours. That number varies widely, so ask every firm on this list for it in the first quote.

choose.h: Match the desk to the industry.
choose.p: Malone separates commercial, professional and healthcare staffing, and Insight Global lists dozens of industries for its Louisville office. Ask to speak with the recruiter who covers your sector, not the general intake line.

inhouse.h: When to keep recruiting in house
p: An agency fee makes sense for a surge you cannot staff yourself, such as peak season at a fulfillment center or a six month finance system project. Professionals who already have jobs rarely answer postings, so teams that keep hiring in house need a way to reach them directly. Noon is one option that finds candidates and runs personalized email and SMS outreach, which some recruiting teams use alongside or instead of an outside firm. For a wider view of the market, see our staffing and recruiting firms list.

h1: Architecture recruiting firms: 7 search partners for studios, AEC firms and builders
seoTitle: Architecture Recruiting Firms: 7 Checked (2026)
description: Seven architecture recruiting firms checked November 21, 2026: who recruits designers, who runs AEC leadership searches, who fills contract BIM seats, and how their fee models differ.
lead: A 40 person studio losing its only healthcare project architect, a national AEC firm planning who will own the Denver office in five years, and a contractor that wants a licensed architect running preconstruction all say they need an architecture recruiter. They should not call the same one. Some firms on this list recruit only designers and read portfolios for a living, some are management consultancies that run a handful of leadership searches each year, and some are construction headhunters with an architecture desk. We checked each firm's own website on November 21, 2026 and describe only what they publish about themselves.
shortAnswer: Short answer: for designers, interior designers and landscape architects, start with Bespoke Careers or DAVRON. For a principal, partner or studio leader tied to succession or a merger, look at Zweig Group or CSG Talent. For architects working on the contractor or owner side, try Construction Hunters or Raymond Search Group, and for contract BIM and CAD help, Apollo Technical.

choose.h: Write down the building type before the title.
choose.p: A project architect with ten years of K12 work and one with ten years of luxury residential are different candidates. Recruiters that organize by sector, like CSG Talent, will ask this first. If yours does not, tell them anyway, because it narrows the pool more than license status or software skills.

choose.h: Ask who will review portfolios.
choose.p: Design hires are judged on work samples. Find out whether the person screening candidates has worked in a studio or simply forwards PDFs. Bespoke Careers says its recruiters include former architects and designers; for other firms, ask for the name of the consultant and their background.

choose.h: Pick contingency or retained on purpose.
choose.p: Contingency means you pay only if you hire through the firm, and you can use several firms at once. Retained means an exclusive search with part of the fee paid up front, which is common for principals and studio directors. DAVRON offers both, which makes it easy to compare.

choose.h: Match the firm to which side of the table the role sits on.
choose.p: An architect inside a design practice, an architect managing design for a general contractor and an owner's representative need different networks. Construction focused search firms reach the second and third groups better than design recruiters do.

firms.name: Bespoke Careers
firms.model: Architecture and design recruitment, permanent and contract
firms.hq: Offices in the US, UK, Australia and New Zealand
firms.bestFor: Studios hiring architects, interior designers and landscape architects who want a recruiter that only works in design
firms.summary: Bespoke Careers is the only firm on this list whose whole business is architecture and design. Lindsay Urquhart founded it in Sydney in 2004, and the company now recruits across the UK, the US, Australia and New Zealand; its New York office marked ten years in 2024. The about page describes the recruiting team as architects, designers and specifiers who moved into recruitment, which matters when a hiring partner wants someone who can read a portfolio rather than scan a resume for software names. Beyond placements, the site publishes a salary guide, a salary calculator, 2026 market reports and a city comparison tool, and it runs a confidential salary survey each year. Employers can submit a vacancy directly, and candidates can drop a CV and portfolio for future roles.
good: You are hiring designers whose portfolio matters more than their title
You want salary benchmarks from a recruiter that tracks design pay every year
watch: Its US presence is centered on a few large metros, so ask about coverage in your city
Construction side roles such as superintendents are outside its focus

firms.name: DAVRON
firms.model: Executive search, contingency and retained
firms.bestFor: Firms that hire architects alongside engineers and construction managers and want one search partner for all three
firms.summary: DAVRON is a Tampa recruiting firm that has worked since 1997 across engineering, architecture, construction and manufacturing. Its architecture page frames the work as executive search and headhunting for architectural firms, and the site offers both contingency and retained search, so you can choose whether you pay only on placement or commit to an exclusive search. There is a separate page for landscape architecture, plus city pages for architecture staffing in markets such as Atlanta, Austin and Albuquerque. DAVRON also sells outplacement services, which is unusual for a search firm and useful if a restructuring and a rebuild are happening in the same year.
good: You need landscape architects as well as building architects
You want to pick between contingency and retained terms with the same firm
watch: Engineering is the larger share of its work, so confirm who on the team handles design roles
Outplacement and search sit in one company, so ask how candidate conflicts are handled

firms.name: Zweig Group
firms.model: AEC management consulting with an executive search practice
firms.bestFor: Principals filling leadership seats, such as a studio director or a future owner, in architecture, engineering and construction firms
firms.summary: Zweig Group is better known in the AEC world for research and advice than for recruiting. It publishes The Zweig Letter, runs salary, fee and financial performance surveys for design firms, hosts the ElevateAEC conference and the Principals Academy, and gives out the Hot Firm and Best Firms to Work For awards. Executive search is one of its services, listed next to ownership transition, valuation, mergers and strategic planning. That combination fits a particular kind of hire: a principal or studio leader whose arrival is tied to an ownership plan or a merger. Zweig lists offices in Dallas and Fayetteville, Arkansas.
good: The hire is connected to succession, an acquisition or a new office
You already use Zweig compensation data and want a search team that shares it
watch: Not built for volume hiring of project architects or drafters
Consulting and search come from the same firm, so keep the two scopes separate in your contract

firms.name: Raymond Search Group
firms.model: Executive search for the built environment
firms.bestFor: Design build firms and developers hiring architecture leaders who also need construction or MEP hires
firms.summary: Raymond Search Group describes itself as an executive search firm built only for the built environment. Architecture sits on its specialty list with construction and real estate, engineering, HVAC/R, building automation, water technology, data centers, power and private equity. The site notes recognition as a Forbes America's Best Recruiting Firm and publishes guides for both clients and candidates, including an overview of its search process. For an architecture practice, the main appeal is breadth across the project team: if a data center or healthcare program needs a design leader and a building systems lead at the same time, one firm can run both searches.
good: Your project mix includes data centers, MEP heavy work or private equity backed owners
You want one search firm for design and building systems roles
watch: Architecture is one of many specialties, so ask for recent design placements
Its site does not list a fee model, so get terms in writing early

firms.name: CSG Talent
firms.model: Global executive search with an architecture desk
firms.hq: International, with US executive search pages by state
firms.bestFor: Practices hiring senior architects for a specific sector such as healthcare, education or workplace interiors
firms.summary: CSG Talent is a global executive search firm whose building and infrastructure practice includes a dedicated architecture recruitment page. That page organizes senior hiring by market sector: commercial, higher education and K12, healthcare and life sciences, hospitality, mixed use, residential and workplace interiors. Sorting by sector is the right instinct for this field, because a hospital planner and a hospitality designer rarely share a shortlist. CSG also recruits in construction, civil engineering, building materials and facilities management, and it publishes state level executive search pages for markets such as California, Florida and Massachusetts.
good: You need a senior hire with deep experience in one building type
You are hiring across borders or opening an office abroad
watch: Focus is senior and executive roles, not junior designers
Architecture is one desk inside a large multi industry firm

firms.model: Contract, contract to hire and direct hire recruiting
firms.bestFor: Southeastern and Texas firms that need CAD and BIM technicians or project support on contract
firms.summary: Apollo Technical recruits engineering, IT and supply chain talent and lists architectural firms among the 26 industries it serves. Its headquarters is in Smyrna, Georgia, with recruiters covering Dallas and Fort Worth, Houston, Austin and San Antonio, Tampa and Orlando, Raleigh and Charlotte, Columbia and Greenville, and Chicago. For an architecture office, Apollo fits technical and support seats more naturally than design leadership, for example a Revit technician for a deadline crunch or a contract project coordinator.
good: You want a contractor this month, not a search that runs a quarter
Your office is in one of its Sun Belt metros
watch: Architecture is a small part of a mostly engineering and IT book
Not the choice for a design principal or studio director search

firms.name: Construction Hunters
firms.model: Executive search and recruiting
firms.bestFor: General contractors and owners hiring architects for preconstruction, design management or owner side roles
firms.summary: Construction Hunters is a Dallas executive search firm serving construction, architecture, engineering and real estate. Its about page says its consultants have built contacts with general contractors, architectural firms, engineering firms and real estate companies across North America, and that it focuses on passive candidates who are busy in their current jobs. The firm runs an architecture practice with location pages, including one for New York. It was co-founded by Craig Robins of Robins Consulting, whose background is in transportation and logistics recruiting. The fit is strongest where the architect will sit on the builder or owner side of the table rather than inside a design studio.
good: The architect will work for a contractor, developer or owner
You want a firm that already recruits project managers and estimators for the same team
watch: Studio design roles are not its core
Ask which recruiter covers architecture, since most of its work is construction

inhouse.h: When to recruit architects yourself
p: Studios with a recognizable portfolio often get strong applicants from their own careers page, AIA chapter job boards and school relationships, especially for entry level designers. A recruiter fee is harder to justify for those seats than for a licensed project architect with a specific sector history, where the people you want are employed and not reading job ads.

If you keep hiring in house, plan for direct outreach. Make a short list of firms whose work resembles yours, look for the people credited on those projects, and contact them with a note about a specific project rather than a generic posting. Our sourcing tools category covers contact finders and outreach software that help with this, and the staffing and recruiting firms list covers generalist agencies for administrative and support seats.

sections.h: Which firm fits which architecture hire
p: Junior and mid level designers: Bespoke Careers and DAVRON. Both publish dedicated architecture pages, and DAVRON adds a landscape architecture practice.

Principals, partners and studio leaders: Zweig Group, CSG Talent and Raymond Search Group. Zweig ties search to ownership and merger work, CSG sorts by building sector, and Raymond covers design and building systems leadership together.
Contract technical support: Apollo Technical, which offers contract and contract to hire placements and advertises a 10 to 15 day average time to fill.
Architects on the builder or owner side: Construction Hunters and Raymond Search Group.

faq.q: What does an architecture recruiting firm do?
faq.a: It finds and screens candidates for architecture and design roles, from junior designers to principals, and presents a shortlist to the hiring firm. Some also offer contract staffing for technical roles such as BIM and CAD work.

faq.q: How much do architecture recruiters charge?
faq.a: Most firms on this list do not publish fees. Contingency search is usually charged as a percentage of first year salary on hire, and retained search splits the fee into installments, part paid before candidates are presented. Ask each firm for written terms and a replacement guarantee.

faq.q: Do architecture recruiters place interior designers and landscape architects?

h1: HVAC staffing agencies: 9 firms for service techs, install crews and mechanical leaders
